title: Developing Safe and Responsible Large Language Model : Can We Balance Bias Reduction and Language Understanding ?
findings: The proposed instruction fine-tuned model (SR_LLM) effectively reduces stereotypical bias related to religion while preserving language understanding. In the StereoSet evaluation for the religion category, SR_LLM achieved a high ICAT score (77.24), indicating a strong balance between low stereotype bias (SS of 62.23, where 50 is neutral) and high language quality (LMS of 93.99). In the Toxigen evaluation, SR_LLM also demonstrated low toxicity scores when generating content related to specific religious groups like Muslims and Jews, performing comparably to or better than models like GPT-4.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the reduction of stereotypical bias and toxicity related to religious groups. It used the StereoSet benchmark to evaluate stereotype scores (SS), language modeling scores (LMS), and Idealized Context Association Test (ICAT) scores for the 'Religion' category. It also used the Toxigen dataset to measure the percentage of toxic content generated for specific religious groups.
